gallery.description:
Image Number: 3-1-1-007
Davis Flat 2500ft. 8 mi N of Dunlop, Fresno Co. 5 mi S. of Kings River Entrance to bear (hibernating) den in boulder pile. This crack was 2 feet wide, 6 feet deep and 10 feet long. At the furthur end the passageway turned abruptly to the left and entered the den proper which was 40 inches wide 50 inches high and 60 inches long. Used by female and her two cubs of the previous season. See notes. J.D. p. 1681

gallery.title: File:Giant sequoia - DPLA - 4802cb730752c530d639d3ebc926f09a.jpg
gallery.description: A log cabin can be seen through the base of a giant sequoia tree at Yosemite National Park in California. Edmund F. Arras (7/7/1875-10/19/1951), a prominent Columbus businessman and entrepreneur, founded one of the city’s first property rental agencies in 1892. Trained as a lawyer, he graduated from OSU law school in 1896 and went on to hold positions in numerous civic groups around the city. He was particularly active within Kiwanis International and was involved with several local religious organizations. In 1913, he and his wife Elizabeth traveled to the World Sunday School Association Convention in Zurich, Switzerland. They continued on to travel extensively throughout Europe documenting their journey through photographs. Due to the timing of their trip, these photos comprise a valuable collection of images of European cities later devastated by war. The Arras family’s lantern slides and negatives include images from their 1913 travels through US east coast cities, Atlantic islands of the Azores, Madeira, Gibraltar and the countries of Algeria, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, England, and Ireland. Also included are images from their 1920 train journey from Chicago to the western US for the Kiwanis Convention in Portland and a 1924 trip to the Denver Kiwanis Convention with stops in Arizona, the Pacific Coast, Canada and New England Coast states. By June of 1924, Arras and his wife had visited every US state and province of Canada. He retired as Kiwanis president in July 1924.
